content: Decreased skin pigmentation can be categorized into two distinct phenomena: hypopigmentation and depigmentation. Understanding the difference between these two is critical for establishing an accurate differential diagnosis. Depigmentation refers to the complete loss of pigment in the skin, resulting in areas that are entirely devoid of color. This is often associated with conditions such as vitiligo, where melanocytes are destroyed or absent. Hypopigmentation, on the other hand, describes a reduction in pigment, leading to lighter skin areas that still retain some degree of color. This can occur in conditions such as post-inflammatory hypopigmentation or certain genetic disorders affecting melanin production. Both hypopigmentation and depigmentation can provide important diagnostic clues, whether the presentation is localized to specific areas or generalized across the body.
